Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.picker

Class PickerGate

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.picker.PickerGate
public final class PickerGate extends Object
Server-side authorization and throttling for client-driven picker operations — the two halves of the same gate, always checked together by the packet handlers.

Authorization (mayUsePicker(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player)) is creative mode plus permission level 2, the level of vanilla /summon, /tp, and /fill: the picker freezes, moves, and spawns mobs and can rewrite blocks without firing the events protection mods listen to, so it is an operator tool. The client CLI and keyboard picker apply the same rule as UX only and are never trusted; packet handlers use authorized(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer), which refuses silently so unauthorized custom-payload spam cannot amplify into server feedback packets.

Every picker throttle lives here: one request per player per tick, the server-wide spawn-all cooldown, and the two export limits. Each successful export triggers a full datapack reload, so successes have the longer EXPORT_COOLDOWN_TICKS; every attempt has the short EXPORT_ATTEMPT_COOLDOWN_TICKS, applied before any codec work. Per-player state is released when the player leaves and all of it at server stop, since getTickCount restarts from 0 with the next (single-player) world and a stale large tick would read as a far-future cooldown.
